subject.title: Feature: Floating agent bubbles (Clawi) for macOS

question: Should the core macOS app own configurable floating per-agent bubbles, or should OpenClaw first define a native UI/window extension seam for an external implementation?
rationale: Current main has the underlying native app, activity, and chat surfaces but no product contract for persistent floating windows, input behavior, persistence ownership, or per-agent bubble lifecycle.

options.title: Build optional core feature
options.body: Add a disabled-by-default native macOS bubble experience using canonical activity and session routing, with focused accessibility and persistence design.

options.title: Create extension seam first
options.body: Expose a supported native macOS UI/window contract so a separately maintained plugin or companion can implement the experience without private imports.

options.title: Decline floating windows
options.body: Keep the existing menu-bar, status, and WebChat surfaces as the supported macOS interaction model and close the request as not planned.

recommendation.title: Build optional core feature
recommendation.body: Add a disabled-by-default native macOS bubble experience using canonical activity and session routing, with focused accessibility and persistence design.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature lineage and adjacent native macOS UI ownership are strongest in this person’s merged history.
